title: Revisiting ensemble methods for stock and crypto trading (Holzer, Wang, Xiao, Liu; ACM ICAIF FinRL)
why: Full text read for S10-3 Q3. Uses BOTH rules: stock task averages action probabilities (Sharpe-softmax weights) and its best ensemble did not beat PPO on return (62.60% vs 63.37%); crypto task majority-votes actions and beats all individuals, but over a 45-minute OOS window, with 'near identical' members from lack of diversity (KL diversity term used). Corrects the 06 knowledge line: only the crypto half votes over actions.

title: Conservative Q-Learning for offline RL (Kumar, Zhou, Tucker, Levine; NeurIPS 2020)
why: 010 step 2. Lower-bound Q against overestimation from distributional shift; discrete variant on QR-DQN evaluated on Atari. Gains largest on MIXED datasets (medium-expert, random-expert), small on single-policy data; narrow expert data caused 'unlearning' in policy-constraint methods; Q-training has no state shift but the policy may at test time. -> 010 offline dataset must be mixed (oracle+clone+perturbed+random).

title: Offline RL with Implicit Q-Learning (Kostrikov, Nair, Levine; 2021)
why: 010 step 2/3. Never queries unseen actions (expectile regression + advantage-weighted extraction); evaluated on continuous control only; notes an upper expectile can chase 'lucky' stochastic transitions; explicitly supports online fine-tuning after offline init -> replaces PPO as 010 step 3.

title: Decision Transformer (Chen et al.; NeurIPS 2021)
why: Percentile BC (clone top X% trajectories) matches offline RL when data is plentiful - 06 is roughly a hindsight %BC, so the bar for offline RL is high. CQL fails when return is delayed to the final step while DT/%BC do not -> 010 drops the terminal Q from the reward. Choosing the %BC cut needs rollouts -> region width is a trial. Not adopted (dense reward kept).

title: Reinforcement learning for trading (Moody & Saffell; NIPS 1998)
why: Read in place of the unreachable 2001 IEEE TNN paper. Differential Sharpe + recurrent RL; yearly retrain on moving 20y window with validation early stopping; 25y ex-ante test at 0.5% cost; committee majority vote of 30 RRL traders Sharpe 0.83 vs buy-and-hold 0.34; Q-trader trained on bootstrap samples. Precedent for vote-over-positions and walk-forward-by-year.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for trading (Zhang, Zohren, Roberts; JFDS 2020)
why: Discrete {-1,0,1} actions, DQN best overall; volatility-scaled profit reward with cost term in the reward (bp treated as a turnover regulariser); 50 futures 2011-2019, retrained every 5 years; DQN and A2C still profitable at 25bp cost. Supports small discrete action space and cost-in-reward.

title: A deep RL framework for the financial portfolio management problem (Jiang, Xu, Liang; 2017)
why: Crypto (Poloniex, 30-min, 0.25% commission). Previous portfolio weights fed back into the state so the agent sees transaction costs -> supports book state. Backtests ~50 days each; authors name zero market impact and zero slippage as the main weakness.

title: FinRL Contests: benchmarking data-driven financial RL agents (Wang et al.; 2025)
why: The published FinRL out-of-sample record: 2023 teams negative in the second test week, 'generalization to new, unseen market conditions remains a challenge'; crypto winners +0.23% (2024) and -0.05% (2025) over ~2 days of second-level data. No multi-year cost-inclusive OOS record -> 010 stays offline-first and gated on validation years.

title: DRL for cryptocurrency trading: practical approach to address backtest overfitting (Gort, Liu et al.; 2022)
why: Walk-forward 'validates in one market situation' and a single validation set 'can easily result in model overfitting'; uses combinatorial CV and rejects agents with probability of backtest overfitting above 10%. -> 010 adds PBO over the trial ledger with a 10% rejection.

title: When should we prefer offline RL over behavioral cloning? (Kumar, Hong, Singh, Levine; ICLR 2022)
why: Offline RL beats BC with noisy suboptimal data on long horizons, or when few states are 'critical'; several works found BC better than offline RL. -> supports clone-then-offline-RL order and the region idea (critical states concentrated).

title: Realistic market impact modeling for RL trading environments (Abbade & Costa; 2026)
why: Square-root impact changes the ranking of algorithms -> 010 must use the backtester's full costs. Reward DSR - lambda_dd*(dDD+)^2 but lambda tuned by Optuna on OOS Sharpe (selection on test), no value reported in text read. PPO in-sample up while OOS declines over epochs -> argues against PPO as step 3.

title: Decomposable reward modeling and realistic environment design for RL Forex trading (Saidd; 2026)
why: 11-component reward incl. drawdown weight 0.05; results on training period only and non-monotone; states finance penalties such as drawdown are not policy-invariant (citing Ng 1999); 3-action adapter had higher Sharpe/lower DD than 10-action; legal-action masking in training and replay -> adopted by 010.

title: Deep policy gradient methods in commodity markets (Hanetho; thesis 2023)
why: Nearest published lambda sweep: net log return minus lambda*variance(60), lambda in {0,0.01,0.1,0.2}, OOS natural gas 2017-2022 net of costs; 0.01 best Sharpe, larger lambda cut returns 25-38%. Variance, not drawdown - evidence of shape, not a value for 010.

title: Multimodal deep RL for portfolio optimization (Nawathe et al.; 2024)
why: Differential Sharpe vs profit reward, test 2018-2019: DSR 'a difficult reward', underperformed profit, but 'difficult for a model to overfit'. Caveat for 010's DSR arm.

title: Statistical overfitting and backtest performance (Bailey, Ger, Lopez de Prado, Sim, Wu)
why: Read in place of the bot-blocked AMS Notices 2014 paper; reports its result: with 5 years of daily data, 45+ independent variations make a Sharpe >= 1.0 winner likely by chance; hold-out does not control the number of trials. -> 010 trial ledger.

title: Deep reinforcement learning that matters (Henderson et al.; AAAI 2018)
why: Two groups of 5 seeds with identical hyperparameters gave statistically different distributions; averaging N<5 trials can mislead. -> 010 raises seeds 4 -> 5 for gated comparisons, spread always reported.

title: Notes on Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning (ch. 7, 11-14)
why: Secondary notes (book not opened): purging/embargo; walk-forward 'very easy to overfit because only 1 history is tested'; CPCV tests alternative histories; 'every backtest must be reported with all trials involved in its production'. -> 010 embargo sized by label span, trial ledger.

title: The recurrent reinforcement learning crypto agent (Borrageiro, Firoozye, Barucca; 2022)
why: Direct RRL on XBTUSD perpetual, 5 bps fees, +350% over ~5 years net of costs, but 71% of return is funding profit - not evidence of a trading edge; context only.
